notes: Workers Free plan CPU time limit is 10 ms per invocation (HTTP request and Cron Trigger); Workers Paid default is 30 s per HTTP request, configurable up to 5 min (300,000 ms). Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/

Workers Free daily request limit is 100,000/day, resetting at midnight UTC; requests beyond the cap return Error 1027 (or bypass the Worker if fail-open is configured). Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/

Workers AI free allocation is PER DAY: 10,000 Neurons/day at no charge on both Free and Paid, resetting at 00:00 UTC; beyond that, Paid is billed at $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons and Free fails with an error. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/

R2 egress is free ($0) on all storage classes. R2 free tier (10 GB-month, 1M Class A, 10M Class B per month) applies to Standard storage only and is monthly, not daily. The R2 pricing page does not state whether a free account is blocked or billed beyond the free tier; the cf.r2.* free.overage values are placeholders and those meters are marked unverified for that reason only (all numeric values are verified).
Workers Paid is $5 USD per month minimum. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/
Convention: quota/included = null with overage 'none' and pricePer 0 means unmetered/included, not unknown. Only meters with unverified=true carry an uncertain value.

Overage semantics: 'drop' = individual operations beyond the cap fail with an error; 'block' = the service refuses queries until the daily reset (D1 wording: 'you will not be able to run queries against D1').

Cache, WAF, Bot Fight Mode and rate limiting entitlements are governed by the zone plan (Free/Pro/Business/Enterprise), not the Workers Free/Paid subscription; the Workers Paid plan does not change them.

Durable Objects Free plan supports SQLite-backed objects only; SQLite storage on Free: 5M rows read/day, 100k rows written/day, 5 GB total. Key-Value backend is Paid only. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/
Queues on Workers Free: 10,000 operations/day with 24-hour non-configurable retention; Paid allows retention up to 14 days. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/platform/pricing/
Vectorize stored dimensions is a total-stored figure (5M on Free, 10M included on Paid) rather than monthly consumption; the schema period 'month' is nominal for it.
All values fetched 2026-09-02 from developers.cloudflare.com pages listed in each meter's source field.

Stream, Images storage/delivery, Zaraz Paid, Zero Trust (Access) and Load Balancing are separate subscriptions/add-ons; their paid blocks do not depend on the Workers Paid plan. Hyperdrive, Workflows, Browser Rendering, Analytics Engine, Containers and Email Sending follow the Workers Free/Paid plan.

Browser Rendering free quota is 10 minutes/day, stored as 0.1666667 hours/day so the unit matches the paid block (hours). Concurrency ($2.00 per additional browser above 10 on Paid) is not modelled as a meter.

Workers Analytics Engine: Cloudflare states usage is currently not billed; the published numbers are advance notice for cost estimation. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/analytics-engine/pricing/

Workflows invocations and CPU time are billed via the Workers requests/CPU meters; only steps (and storage) are Workflows-specific. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/pricing/

Load Balancing pricing (base price, included DNS queries, per-500k overage) could not be verified: https://developers.cloudflare.com/load-balancing/reference/pricing/ and /pricing-and-plans/ return 404 and the docs defer to the dashboard for pricing. cf.load_balancing.queries paid values are null and the meter is unverified.
Zero Trust Free plan: 50 user limit; Pay-as-you-go $7 per user/month paid annually. Source (cloudflare.com marketing page): https://www.cloudflare.com/zero-trust/products/access/
Containers included vCPU is published as 375 vCPU-minutes/month; cf.containers.vcpu_seconds stores it as 22,500 vCPU-seconds to match the per-second overage unit.
